newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik soldiers killed in clashes with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Tajik soldiers killed in clashes with rebels.

text.p: Several Tajik soldiers were killed when rebels stormed administrative buildings in the regional centre of Garm on Sunday, and the Dushanbe authorities have sent reinforcements to the region, Russian news agencies said.
But communications with the region, some 200 km (130 miles) to the east of the capital of the former Soviet republic, had been severed and it was impossible to determine the extent of the casualties.

Itar-Tass news agency said about 100 rebels had attacked the buildings, setting some of them ablaze. "There are dead and wounded among the governent forces, but the exact figure is not clear because there are no communications with the town."

Tajik government troops, backed by Russian border forces, have been struggling to crack down on the opposition in the impoverished former Soviet republic, which borders Afghanistan, China, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.
Islamic guerrillas launch frequent raids on Tajikistan from bases inside Afghanistan and there have been attacks on Russian soldiers in Dushanbe itself, despite a series of peace deals.
Other rebels have waged a guerrilla war against the Dushanbe authorities since their defeat in a 1992 civil war.
"The latest incident is a gross violation of all peace accords," Interfax news agency quoted a Tajik military source as saying.
Tens of thousands have died and many more have lost their homes in a civil war which devastated Tajikistan after independence in September, 1991.
